subject: Customer-crafted output license & retrain limits — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlift.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: salesops@starlift.com; kevin.li@starlift.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify output ownership & retrain rights in MSA/Order Form

Irene — thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team had a few focused asks on IP and productization:

1) Output ownership: we need a clear statement that any customer-provided data and outputs generated from that data remain the customer’s property, and Redwood cannot re-sell or otherwise market those outputs.
2) Retraining / model use: Starlift will not consent to our data being used to retrain or fine-tune Redwood models unless we opt in per model and per project.
3) Feedback license: we need to limit the license for feedback (bug reports, usage telemetry) to non-personally-identifying aggregated telemetry only; no general feedback license that would allow model improvement using Starlift content.

Can you confirm whether the current redline (Exhibit B) can be adjusted to reflect those constraints? We’re happy to agree to a narrow operations-safe clause (e.g., for latency improvements) but not open-ended retraining or productization rights.

Thanks —
Maria
Maria Gomez
General Counsel, Starlift Inc.

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlift.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com; karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify output ownership & retrain rights in MSA/Order Form

Maria —

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached a short redline (Redline_MSAA_20260719.docx) and a proposed Exhibit B PDF that tries to strike the balance you describe. Key highlights:

- Output ownership: Exhibit B now states "Customer retains title to Customer Data and Customer Output; Redwood will not assert ownership or commercialize Customer Output except with Customer’s prior written consent."
- Retraining: we’ve added an opt-in framework — Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train or improve models unless Starlift provides an explicit written opt-in for specific projects/models and the parties agree on scope and compensation.
- Feedback license: replaced the broad feedback grant with a "Limited Telemetry License" that allows Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for reliability and service improvement only; model training explicitly excluded.

Iager (internal): can you and Laura review the cost and operational implications of locking retrain-out by default? Laura — I flagged the potential impact to our "model improvement" program and on pricing for larger customers if we move to an opt-in+paid retainer model.

If Starlift is comfortable with the language in Exhibit B (PDF attached), we can push the redline back to their counsel and propose a short SOW addendum if they decide to opt in to training at a later date.

Next steps:
- Starlift to review redline and confirm whether the wording is acceptable or they want narrower carveouts.
- If they want to opt in to training, we propose a separate SOW and fee schedule (I’ll attach a template once we hear back).

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redline_MSAA_20260719.docx; Exhibit-B-output-license-draft.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com; laura.bennett@redwood.com; karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing & ops impact for retrain opt-in

Team — quick note on the commercial side after reading Irene’s redline:

- If we make retrain opt-in by default, we should bake in a tiered surcharge for any customer-requested retraining projects (covers compute, annotation, and IP/admin overhead).
- Offer a "Training Credit" in the order form (prepaid hours) that can be consumed when the customer opts in. That keeps baseline ARR predictable.
- Operational: ops will need an intake and approval workflow for any retrain SOWs (security review, data scoping, logging). That’s non-trivial — Karhtik, can infra estimate the runbook/budget?

Willing to propose 3 pricing bands (Pilot, Production retrain, Dedicated retrain) and a draft SOW template.

—Ben
VP, Revenue Operations

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>; laura.bennett@redwood.com; irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-20T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: pricing & ops impact for retrain opt-in

Ben — I can scope the infra/runbook: rough estimate to support opt-in retraining workflow (security review, enclave provisioning, audit trail, cost attribution) is ~4 engineer-weeks + 2 SREs for ongoing support (initial ramp). We’ll need a standard data ingestion checklist (Starlift-data-map.xlsx) and a small automation to tag datasets that are "opt-in" so they don’t bleed into general training buckets.

If legal wants to keep retrain-out as default, ops can support opt-in but we should include a minimum fee (to cover the provisioning + compliance review).

Will draft a short ops appendix we can attach to the SOW.

—Karthik
Director, Platform Reliability

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlift.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com; karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final: proposed compromise language and next steps (MSA Exhibit B)

Maria — following up with our agreed compromise and next steps.

Summary of confirmed positions (per Exhibit B attached):
- Customer Output: Starlift retains title to Customer Data and Customer Output. Redwood will not commercialize or market Customer Output without Starlift’s prior written consent.
- Retraining: Default: no use for model training or improvement. Option: Starlift may opt in to specific retrain projects via a separate SOW. That SOW will define scope, model(s), timeline, data handling, and fees. Redwood will not use opt-in data outside that SOW.
- Telemetry/feedback: Redwood may process aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service reliability and bug fixes only. Any use of customer content for model improvement is expressly excluded without opt-in.

Attachments: final redline (Redline_MSAA_20260719.docx) and Exhibit-B-output-license-draft.pdf. If this matches Starlift’s expectation, please confirm and we’ll circulate a clean MSA+Order Form for signatures and attach a sample SOW template that includes the pricing bands Karthik/Ben mentioned.

Thanks for the productive dialogue — we aimed to preserve your protections while keeping an operationally viable path for authorized retrain projects.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0133
